# ANALYSIS: Walk-forward OOS and Real-fills Check on Top 3 J Days

**Filed:** 2026-07-07  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** quality_gate  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

We need to verify that any candidate strategy’s edge_capture is stable across walk-forward out-of-sample (OOS) windows and that real-fills simulation on the three J anchor days deviates by less than 20% from the BS-sim baseline. This ensures the strategy is not overfit to the limited J sample and will survive realistic execution slippage.

## Mechanism

1. **Walk-forward OOS test:** Split the available 16-month history into expanding windows (e.g., train 12 months, test 4 months) rolling forward; compute edge_capture on each OOS window and require the average OOS edge_capture ≥ 0.8 × in-sample edge_capture (i.e., <20% degradation).  
2. **Real-fills check:** For each of the three J days (4/29, 5/01, 5/04), run the strategy through a realistic OPRA simulator (bid/ask, slippage, latency) and compare the P&L to the BS-sim baseline; require the absolute percent difference <20% on each day.  
3. **Stability criterion:** If both tests pass, the strategy’s edge_capture is considered stable; otherwise, it is rejected or sent back for refinement.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 (max observed in J winners) requires $25K+ account per risk-rules.md; $1K paper account ≈14% of headline P&L.  
2. **Sample bias:** Only three J anchor days are used for OP-16 edge_capture; this is an extremely small sample (n=3) with high overfit risk. Any strategy tuned to these days may fail catastrophically on unseen regimes.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward held-out window not yet performed).  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (realistic OPRA simulation on top 3 J days not yet performed).  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day could be a large loser exceeding the per-trade 50% risk cap; max drawdown could exceed 30% of equity if the strategy takes losers on non-J days; blow-up scenario involves consecutive losses on high-VIX days where premium stops are breached due to gap risk.  
6. **Concentration:** Unknown; requires analysis of P&L distribution across the 16-month sample to determine what percentage of total edge_capture comes from the top‑5 days.
